Its candidate order is an explicit BATON_V12_DISK_ROOT operand first, then tempfile.gettempdir(), then the distribution root, then /var/tmp -- and it REFUSES rather than silently falling back if an explicit variable names memory-backed or unwritable storage.
the_mechanism_the_turn_introduced.what_it_ran_into: the root it found has bounded space. The composed runtime profile bounds scratch at tmp_bytes 67108864 and shm_bytes 16777216 with workspace_min_bytes 83886081, and 864 cases each creating SQLite stores exhausted whatever root was chosen.
the_mechanism_the_turn_introduced.why_it_is_the_right_shape: the verifier exports TMPDIR as a /proc/self/fd alias over scratch, and scratch is memory-backed, so the production boundary correctly refuses a workspace there. The helper states the choice instead of skipping, which is the rule this Work is about.
